title: Division Java Will Not Warn You About
statement:
Java's `int` arithmetic never throws on overflow -- `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`
and `%` all wrap silently, every time, with no `checked` context to opt
into the way some other languages have. `b == 0` is the one division
failure Java *does* police for you, throwing `ArithmeticException`. The
other classic division failure -- `Integer.MIN_VALUE / -1`, whose true
result does not fit in 32 bits -- is not policed at all: Java just hands
back `Integer.MIN_VALUE` again, silently, as if nothing had gone wrong.

## The types

Provided by the harness, visible to your solution without an import
(same package):

```
enum DivideStatus { OK, DIVIDE_BY_ZERO, OVERFLOW }
record DivideResult(DivideStatus status, int value) {}
```

## Your function

```
public static DivideResult safeDivide(int a, int b);
```

Divide `a` by `b`, reporting which of three things happened:

- **`b == 0`** -- return `new DivideResult(DivideStatus.DIVIDE_BY_ZERO, 0)`.
- **`a == Integer.MIN_VALUE && b == -1`** -- return
  `new DivideResult(DivideStatus.OVERFLOW, 0)`. `Integer.MIN_VALUE` is
  `-2147483648`; its magnitude has no positive `int` counterpart
  (`Integer.MAX_VALUE` is only `2147483647`), so the mathematically
  correct result of this division, `2147483648`, cannot be represented as
  an `int` at all.
- **Otherwise** -- return `new DivideResult(DivideStatus.OK, a / b)`,
  ordinary Java integer division (which truncates towards zero, not
  towards negative infinity).

## Watch out

- **`Integer.MIN_VALUE / -1` does not throw in Java.** It does not throw
  `ArithmeticException`, it does not throw anything -- it silently
  evaluates to `Integer.MIN_VALUE` again, the same wrong-looking value
  you started with, with nothing in the language telling you an overflow
  just happened. A solution that only wraps the division in a `try` and
  catches whatever it can, hoping to detect this case that way, catches
  nothing: there is no exception to catch. The check has to be an
  explicit `if`, run *before* the division, not a reaction to anything
  the division itself does.
- **This is a genuinely separate failure from `b == 0`.** Nothing about
  `b == -1` looks like a division by zero, and reporting every problem
  division as `DIVIDE_BY_ZERO` -- reusing the one case Java actually
  throws for -- reports the wrong reason for a failure that has nothing
  to do with zero at all.
- **Every other input, including `Integer.MIN_VALUE` divided by anything
  other than `-1`, is `OK`.** `Integer.MIN_VALUE / 1` is
  `Integer.MIN_VALUE`, representable and unremarkable; it is specifically
  the combination of `Integer.MIN_VALUE` as the dividend *and* `-1` as the
  divisor that overflows.
